# WO-2026-08-15-06 — canonical ding callers, and a runtime checker that stops lying

**Two small, independent defects. Both narrow. ⛔ Warwick's words: "Keep this narrow. Do not create another
convergence framework, inventory service, registry or watcher."** If you find yourself building, stop.

## PART A — repo code must stop calling a script that lives outside Git

`C:\.fusion247\larry-ding.mjs` is a **legacy duplicate**. The canonical implementation is
`tools/governor/ding.mjs`, installed at `~/.mypka/governor/ding.mjs`. Two live repository callers still
invoke the legacy one:

- `services/hub/youtube/watch-captures.mjs:78`
- `services/hub/youtube/ensure-youtube-watcher.mjs:164`

both spawning `['--env-file=C:/.fusion247/fusion-capture-gateway.env', 'C:/.fusion247/larry-ding.mjs', tmp]`.

**This was already known and deliberately not fixed.** `Deliverables/2026-08-04-proofline-wayfinder-plan.md`
records it: *"the legacy `C:\.fusion247\larry-ding.mjs` cannot be retired or edited, because that surface is
closed… It remains on disk as a legacy duplicate. Two paths to one channel is a real defect — reported once,
not fixed."* Veritas raised it again as finding 8 in a 4B receipt, non-blocking, "Warwick decides".
**Warwick has now decided: repo callers use canonical.**

**AC1 — Both call sites invoke the canonical installed governor**, not the loose copy.

> **⛔ AMENDED AT READ-BACK, 2026-08-15 — this criterion originally read "The env-file argument stays".
> That was WRONG and it contradicted a higher authority.** Root `CLAUDE.md` § Rule 4a is canonical:
> **"Delivery is `node ~/.mypka/governor/ding.mjs <message-file>` — it loads its own credentials; no
> `--env-file`, no shell preparation."** `ding.mjs` reads its credentials from its own path and ignores
> inherited env for them by design, so the flag was inert — **and actively harmful.** Measured twice
> independently, by the builder and again by Veritas: `node --env-file=<missing> script.mjs` exits **9
> before the script runs**, so a missing env file kills the child with **no accounting line**, defeating
> the load-bearing half of `ding.mjs`. Without the flag the same case exits **2 and writes a durable
> record**. **THE `--env-file` ARGUMENT IS DROPPED.** The stated reason for keeping it — credentials must
> stay out of Git — holds either way: only a path literal ever enters Git.

**AC2 — Prove the canonical script accepts the same invocation.** The callers pass a message FILE path as
the final argument. Confirm `tools/governor/ding.mjs` takes a message-file argument the same way, and say
so with the file:line that proves it. **If the interfaces differ, STOP and report — do not adapt the
caller to a guess.**

**AC3 — No repository file references `C:/.fusion247/larry-ding.mjs` afterwards.** Prove by grep across
the repo, excluding `Deliverables/**`, `Builds/**` and `Team Knowledge/**` where the historical record
legitimately names it. **Do not edit the historical record.**

## PART B — the runtime checker manufactures drift that does not exist

`tools/governor/convergence-runtime-check.ps1` compares an install against canonical using a **raw**
`Get-FileHash` (around lines 98-100) and reports `DERIVED-STALE`. With `core.autocrlf=true` and no root
`.gitattributes` that comparison is **wrong in both directions**, measured today: installed vs **working
tree** falsely differs on **7 of 10** governor modules; installed vs **git blob** falsely differs on
**2 of 10**. All ten are content-identical. **Larry hit this and reported a false convergence finding to
Warwick on the strength of it.**

**AC4 — The checker compares CONTENT, not representation.** Normalise line endings on both sides before
comparing (or compare against the exact blob the install records itself as made from — the install's own
`INSTALLED-FROM.txt` states the route). **Whatever you choose, a file that differs ONLY by line endings
must NOT be reported as drift.**

**AC5 — It still detects REAL drift.** This is the half that matters: a control that reports "clean" for
everything is worse than the false positive it replaced. **Made to fail:** plant a genuine one-character
CONTENT change in a copy of an installed file, prove the checker reports drift for exactly that file,
restore, prove it reports clean. **Report both runs.**

**AC6 — Run it against the REAL current install and report the verdict.** All ten modules are
content-identical today, so a correct checker reports no drift. If it reports drift for something else,
that is a finding — report it, do not fix it here.

**AC7 — No new mechanism.** No new script, no registry, no inventory file, no scheduled task. You are
correcting a comparison inside a file that already exists.
